subject: Hosted API: elevated request queueing in us-east - customer advisory

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API: elevated request queueing in us-east - customer advisory

Hi Maria / Aurelia ops team,

Quick note to let you know we are seeing elevated request queueing in our us-east hosted pool that is affecting p95 request completion for a subset of short-response workloads. We detected the signal at ~08:45 PT and activated our mitigation playbook.

Observed impact:
- Increased p95 latency from ~180ms to ~1.6s for generation endpoints routed to us-east.
- Short bursts of 429s for high-concurrency keys in a narrow time window.

Immediate actions we have taken:
- Enabled temporary throttling on non-critical background routes to prioritize foreground traffic.
- Added an emergency capacity allocation to us-east (20% burst capacity) and routed traffic away from affected instance pool.
- Kicked off a worker restart and KV-cache warm restart for suspected cache thrash.

What this means for Aurelia Health:
- You may see elevated tail latency and occasional transient 429s on some requests while we stabilize.
- No data plane persistence or customer data loss is expected.

We are actively tracking on our incident bridge and will push updates to the status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-11-16-queueing. Attaching a short snapshot of current graphs.

Next update: by 09:45 PT or sooner if we hit full remediation.

Thanks for the quick read — apologies for the interruption.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Hi Maria —

Thanks for the quick reply. Short answers up front: we do not expect the issue to persist into the overnight window but we want to be conservative — if your batch jobs are not latency-sensitive, you should be fine. If they are sensitive to p95 spikes we recommend shifting to our eu region or scheduling a short pause.

Technical update and next steps:
- Root cause signal: We observed a KV-cache eviction storm triggered by a small fleet of workers handling a burst of large-context requests; the eviction caused repeated cache warm misses and increased compute for short requests.
- Mitigations applied: restarted the two worker clusters generating the most eviction pressure, increased KV cache TTLs for short-session routes, and temporarily disabled background prefetch jobs for low-priority tenants.
- Current state: p95 has improved from ~1.6s to ~700ms across the affected slice; error rate (429) has dropped ~80% in the last 20 minutes.

We are keeping an eye on tail behavior and will keep capacity on priority routing for your account over the next 24 hours. If you'd like, we can proactively route your critical keys to a protected capacity pool for the next 48 hours (minor configuration, can be done without disruption).

Also attaching a short timeline CSV for your ops team to correlate with your telemetry.

Marissa Cole
Director, Incident Response, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Hi Maria — following up with a short recap and next steps as we close the active stabilization.

Summary:
- The immediate queueing signal originated 11/16 08:45 PT and stabilized by 11/16 10:00 PT after the mitigations Marissa listed.
- Your traffic experienced short p95 tail elevation during that window; the attached timeline has per-minute spikes we captured.

What we did for Aurelia Health:
- Temporarily routed your keys to a protected capacity pool from 11/16 09:00 PT to 11/18 09:00 PT to ensure steady headroom.
- We increased KV cache TTLs for short-session routes tied to your project id and removed background prefetch on non-critical tenants for 24 hours.
- No persisted data or model-state change occurred.

Postmortem and follow-up:
- We will publish a short incident postmortem on Thursday 11/19 with cause, timeline, and a set of recommended hardening steps (cache sizing, prefetch tuning, and optional protected pool usage).
- Marissa's team will reach out to your engineering contact to schedule a 30-minute incident review if you'd like deeper telemetry.

If you prefer we can proactively schedule your non-latency-sensitive overnight batches to run through eu region for the next week; let me know and we'll coordinate the config change.

Thanks again for the quick coordination — we'll keep the status page updated and send the postmortem link when ready.

Best,
Kimberly Park
